text:
Predicates:
MountainRange(x) ::: x is a mountain range.
LocatedIn(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
Donated(x) ::: x was donated.
Mine(x) ::: x is a mine.
InState(x, y) ::: x is in state y.
HasMine(x, y) ::: mountain range x has mine y.

Premises:
(MountainRange(picurisMountains) ∧ (InState(picurisMountains, newMexico) ∨ InState(picurisMountains, texas))) ::: The Picuris Mountains are a mountain range in New Mexico or Texas.
Visited(juanDeOnate, picurisMountains) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.
Mine(hardingPegmatiteMine) ∧ LocatedIn(hardingPegmatiteMine, picurisMountains) ∧ Donated(hardingPegmatiteMine) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine, located in the Picuris Mountains, was donated.
¬∃x (MountainRange(x) ∧ InState(x, texas) ∧ ∃y (Mine(y) ∧ HasMine(x, y) ∧ Donated(y))) ::: There are no mountain ranges in Texas that have mines which have been donated.

Conclusion:
¬LocatedIn(hardingPegmatiteMine, mountainRangeInNewMexico) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine is not located in a mountain range in New Mexico.
